plt.close()
print("Saved per_layer_dpert.pdf/png")

# ============================================================

# ============================================================
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 3.5))
ax.plot(layers, ks_v2, 'o-', ms=4, lw=1.5, color='#2171B5', label='mvp-001b (easy, n=20)')

md_lines.append(f"**Date**: 2026-05-12\n")
md_lines.append(f"**Experiments**: mvp-001b (v2, 20 easy problems) / mvp-001c (v3, 5 hard problems)\n")

# Table
md_lines.append("## Per-Layer Metrics\n\n")
md_lines.append("| Layer | r (v2) | r (v3) | Δpert% (v2) | Δpert% (v3) | KS (v2) | KS (v3) |\n")
md_lines.append("|------:|-------:|-------:|------------:|------------:|--------:|--------:|\n")
for l in layers:
    sig_v2 = "**" if p_v2[l] < 0.001 else ""
    sig_v3 = "**" if p_v3[l] < 0.001 else ""
    md_lines.append(f"| {l:2d} | {sig_v2}{r_v2[l]:+.4f}{sig_v2} | {sig_v3}{r_v3[l]:+.4f}{sig_v3} | {dpert_v2[l]:+.2f} | {dpert_v3[l]:+.2f} | {ks_v2[l]:.4f} | {ks_v3[l]:.4f} |\n")

md_lines.append(f"\n*Bold = p < 0.001*\n\n")

md_lines.append("## Layer-wise Patterns\n\n")

md_lines.append("### Pearson r by region\n\n")
md_lines.append("| Region | Layers | Mean r (v2) | Mean r (v3) |\n")
md_lines.append("|--------|--------|------------:|------------:|\n")
for name, grp in [("Early", early), ("Mid-Early", mid_early), ("Mid-Late", mid_late), ("Late", late)]:

No layer approaches the ±10% suggestive threshold. The perturbation signal is not concentrated in any specific layer group.\n\n")

md_lines.append(f"5. **KS statistics decline monotonically**: KS stat decreases from ~0.29 (layer 0) to ~0.04 (layer 27) in v2, indicating that MLP activation distribution differences between redundant and novel tokens are strongest in early layers but diminish in deeper layers. This is consistent with early layers performing more generic/surface-level processing.\n\n")

md_lines.append(f"6. **v2 vs v3 consistency**: The per-layer r profiles are highly consistent between easy (v2) and hard (v3) problems (Pearson correlation of profiles: {np.corrcoef(r_v2, r_v3)[0,1]:.3f}). This suggests the signal pattern is model-intrinsic rather than task-dependent.\n\n")

md_lines.append("## Implications for Negative Evidence\n\n")
md_lines.append("- The cross-axis hypothesis predicts that **redundant tokens** (high anchor similarity) should activate MLP neurons less (lower L1 norm) and be more pruneable (higher Δpert). The per-layer analysis shows:\n")

md_lines.append("  - But this signal does NOT translate into differential prunability: Δpert is near-zero across all layers.\n")
md_lines.append("  - The disconnect between Metric 1 (weak positive) and Metric 3/4 (null) suggests that **anchor-based redundancy does not map onto MLP activation sparsity patterns** — the axes are not coupled as hypothesized.\n\n")

with open(f'{OUT_DIR}/analysis_summary.md', 'w') as f:
    f.writelines(md_lines)
print("Saved analysis_summary.md")
print("\nDone. All outputs in:", OUT_DIR)
